```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

```{r}
library(adempR)
```

White, Pham, Quartagno and Morris (2024) describe how to check a
simulation study: check the data-generating mechanism, look at the
estimates before summarizing them, look for outliers and failures, and
check that the standard errors track the variability. adempR has a tool
for each step.

```{r}
study <- sim_study("diagnostics",
  scenarios = sim_scenarios(n = c(15L, 60L), p = c(0.1, 0.4)),
  generate = function(scenario, context) rbinom(scenario$n, 1, scenario$p),
  estimands = list(sim_estimand("prevalence",
                                sim_truth_exact(function(scenario) scenario$p))),
  methods = list(
    wald = function(data) {
      p <- mean(data); se <- sqrt(p * (1 - p) / length(data))
      sim_estimate("prevalence", p, se = se, lower = p - 1.96 * se,
                   upper = p + 1.96 * se, level = 0.95)
    },
    logit = function(data) {
      if (all(data == 0) || all(data == 1)) stop("all outcomes equal")
      f <- glm(data ~ 1, family = binomial)
      ci <- plogis(coef(f) + c(-1.96, 1.96) * sqrt(vcov(f)[1, 1]))
      sim_estimate("prevalence", mean(data), lower = ci[1], upper = ci[2], level = 0.95)
    }),
  measures = c("bias", "coverage", "width"))
```

## Checking the data-generating mechanism

`sim_check_dgp()` generates data sets from each scenario and compares
summaries with their targets using a Bonferroni corrected z test. A flag
means the mechanism does not do what the protocol says; no flag means only
that no discrepancy was detected at this sample size.

```{r}
sim_check_dgp(study, summaries = function(d) c(prevalence = mean(d)),
              targets = function(scenario) c(prevalence = scenario$p), n = 300)
```

## Looking at the run

```{r}
run <- sim_run(study, replications = 300, seed = 2, path = file.path(tempdir(), "diag"))
dx <- sim_diagnose(run)
dx
```

The diagnosis reports failures by method and scenario with their most
common messages, generation failures, outlying estimates by a robust z
score, the association between estimates and their standard errors, any
storage problems, and every revision and amendment.

## Plots

```{r, fig.alt = "Distribution of estimates by method"}
sim_plot(run, "estimates", scenario = 1)
```

The zip plot (Morris et al. 2019) orders intervals by their z statistic
and shows which miss the truth, and on which side.

```{r, fig.alt = "Zip plot of confidence intervals"}
sim_plot(run, "zip", scenario = 1)
```

```{r, fig.alt = "Coverage with Monte Carlo intervals"}
sim_plot(run, "precision", measure = "coverage")
```

```{r, fig.alt = "Failures by scenario and method"}
sim_plot(run, "failures")
```

Other types are `"est_se"` (estimates against standard errors) and
`"runtime"`.

## The report

`sim_report()` writes one self-contained HTML file: aims, protocol,
scenarios (including exclusions), estimands and their truth, methods and
their code, failure policy, execution details, failures, performance with
MCSE, comparisons, diagnostics, the revision and amendment history, and
references. All text from the study is escaped.

```{r}
f <- file.path(tempdir(), "diag-report.html")
sim_report(run, f, overwrite = TRUE)
```

The report describes; it does not interpret. Conclusions are the
author's.

## Export bundles

`sim_export()` writes a directory that someone else can check and reuse
with only adempR installed:

```{r}
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "diag-bundle")
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
sim_export(run, dir)
list.files(dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

`sim_import()` verifies the checksums and returns results that work with
`sim_summarise()`, `sim_compare()` and `sim_report()`. The bundle contains
the study's R code. The checksums detect corruption, not tampering: import
bundles only from sources you trust, as you would source a script.
